key_concepts: A solution forms when a solute dissolves in a solvent into a single uniform phase
Solution particles are too small to be seen and can pass through filters
The solvent is the dissolving component and is usually the larger amount
The solute is the dissolved component and is usually the lesser amount
Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve in a given amount of solvent
A saturated solution contains the maximum amount of dissolved solute
Undissolved excess solid is evidence that a solution is saturated
An unsaturated solution contains less solute than the maximum amount that can dissolve
Adding solute beyond saturation leaves solid at the bottom
35 grams of table salt in 100 mL water forms a saturated solution
